title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 151
paragraphs: Some Greeks also report an event which, in agreement with this account, occurred many years after these things. It so happened that at Susa, the city of Memnon, there were Athenian envoys come about another matter — Callias son of Hipponicus and those who went up with him — and at that same time the Argives had also sent envoys to Susa, who asked Artaxerxes son of Xerxes whether the friendship they had formed with Xerxes still stood, if they themselves wished to maintain it, or whether he now considered them enemies; and King Artaxerxes answered that it most certainly still stood, and that there was no city he reckoned a greater friend than Argos.
